question: Who would not be a violator of the teacher's bed at the time of birth?
premises: Birth involves passage through the mother's womb
Violating the teacher's bed is a grave transgression in convention
The verse uses this as a reductio argument
inference: If conventional impurity logic were applied strictly, everyone would be guilty at birth, showing the absurdity of such judgments.
uncertainties: The rhetorical force depends on traditional associations of guru-talpa-ga
plain_english: When, at the time of birth, who would not be one who violates the teacher's bed?
